text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: private-vpc-agent-heartbeat (AcmeFin-prod) fired (P1) — no heartbeats from onprem-agent for 3m, control-plane unreachable from agent.
pagerduty-bot: Escalation path: oncall -> lead -> infra. Notified kevin.
kevin: ack — I'm on it, pulling logs.
maria: pinging customer slack #acmefin-ops to confirm they didn't change firewall rules.
kevin: quick check: agent host host-71 shows kernel DROPS in conntrack, `iptables` flush done 10m ago? grabbing journal.
kevin: logs from agent: 
```
2026-03-14T02:19:41Z ERROR controlplane: dial tcp 10.12.5.7:443: i/o timeout
2026-03-14T02:20:02Z WARN  heartbeat: missed 5/5 intervals
2026-03-14T02:20:12Z ERROR network: write: connection reset by peer
```
anna: I see recent customer change request: they rolled out a deny policy for ephemeral egress ports at ~02:15 UTC. Could be related.
joel: tagging infra. If their firewall is blocking our agent -> cp traffic, we need either route failover or a temporary port allow.
maria: AcmeFin says they pushed a microseg policy to box fw-03, will check rollback.
kevin: I can try to restart the agent to re-establish conntrack entries, but if firewall blocks, restart won't help long. Preparing restart command.
kevin: running: `systemctl restart redwood-agent` on host-71 — restarting now.
kevin: agent comes back, heartbeat for 45s, then drops again. Looks like packets getting dropped after conntracking times out.
anna: can we switch this customer to the standby control-plane endpoint as a mitigation while they fix firewall?\o joel: yes, we have a regional standby cp in us-west2 for AcmeFin. I can update routing policy for tenant to point at standby.
kevin: running rollout: `redwoodctl tenant update-endpoint --tenant acmefin --endpoint standby-us-west2`
kevin: switched endpoint, agent now connects and syncs KV cache, traffic resumed. Customer telemetry shows request success rate back to 99%.
maria: AcmeFin confirms -- they see RP calls succeeding again. They're rolling back the deny on fw-03 to validate.
joel: good, but we need a durable fix: add a 5-min health-check and auto-rebind to standby if control-plane unreachable 2x in 5m, and add doc for required egress ports.
kevin: filed infra task INF-4821: "auto-failover: tenant agent -> standby cp after repeated heartbeat loss". Linking runbook snippet.
kevin: runbook excerpt pasted: 
```
If agent heartbeat misses >=2 within 5m -> route tenant to standby cp, notify oncall, attempt agent restart once.
Revert when primary control-plane reachable for 10m and agent steady.
```
anna: added temporary note to the incident: customer impact was up to 45s of failed requests during change window, total impacted requests ~1.2k, no data lost.
maria: AcmeFin says they will add allow rule for outbound 443 to control-plane IPs; they'll confirm when done.
kevin: follow-up: we should surface a proactive alert for firewall policy changes in customer-managed NATs — low signal but could reduce noisy P1s. Filing ENG-2079.
joel: escalation and handoff: handing incident to day oncall @anna. I'm off in 20.
anna: taking handoff — I have the mitigation in place, standby routing, and contact with customer. Will monitor 30m then close if stable.
kevin: adding note: we collected packet captures showing TCP FINs from customer firewall after SYN. Attached to incident ticket.
maria: summary for PS/SE: 1) symptom: agent heartbeat -> missed, 2) root cause: customer firewall deny for ephemeral egress ports leading to conntrack resets, 3) mitigation: switched tenant to standby control-plane endpoint, restarted agent, 4) customer action: rollback deny + allow outbound to CP.
joel: thanks team. Closing pager duty alert.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident resolved (AcmeFin-prod) — auto-close triggered after ack & mitigation.
anna: closing thread here with postmortem notes to follow. :white_check_mark:
